issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares numberOfTutors as type int, but the solution implementation declares the field numberOfTutors as short and uses a constructor parameter and setter that accept short. This creates a type inconsistency between the specification and the provided solution (and may confuse students about which numeric type to use for numberOfTutors and what constructor signature to implement).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of numberOfTutors consistent with the UML and problem statement by changing the field, constructor parameter, and setter in the solution to int (i.e., private int numberOfTutors; public Lecture(..., int numberOfTutors) {...} public void setNumberOfTutors(int numberOfTutors) {...}). Alternatively, update the UML/problem statement to explicitly specify short if that was intended. Keeping types consistent prevents confusion about getter/setter signatures and constructor parameters.
